capitals.name: Ras (Stari Ras, near Novi Pazar)
capitals.note: Gazetteer placeholder for the historic site Ras. The Stefan the First-Crowned page has him on 'the throne in Ras' in 1204; for 1188 this is an assumption.

capitals.name: Niš
capitals.note: 'In Niš, in the new capital of Stefan Nemanja, the German emperor and the grand zoupan met at the end of July 1189.' The page does not say how long Niš stayed the capital; 1190 is the year of the Byzantine counter-attack.

capitals.name: Ras (Stari Ras, near Novi Pazar)
capitals.note: Stefan 'returns to the throne in Ras in 1204'; no opened page names a capital for 1191-1203 or 1205-1298, so Ras is carried through. Dragutin's Srem court was at Belgrade (separate state).

capitals.name: Skopje
capitals.note: After the 1299 treaty 'Skopje became kingdoms capital' (Serbian Kingdom page).

rulers.name: Stefan Nemanja
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: Grand župan from 1166 (division of Zavida's sons); 'abdicated the throne in favor of his middle son Stefan' in 1196 (page), so he reigns to 1195 here and Stefan from 1196. Reign years of the list are the researcher's reading of the pages.

rulers.name: Stefan the First-Crowned (Stefan II Nemanjić)
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: 'Stefan had to flee the country in 1202 to the ruler of Bulgaria'; Vukan ruled in his place until 1204 (the Kaloyan page: Vukan 'expelled his brother, Stefan, from Serbia in 1202').

rulers.name: Vukan Nemanjić
rulers.title: Grand Prince
rulers.note: 'Stefan had to flee the country in 1202'; Vukan ruled in his place until 1204 (the Kaloyan page: Vukan 'expelled his brother, Stefan, from Serbia in 1202'). [Review eu-18-c fix: gap 1202-1203 filled.]

rulers.name: Stefan the First-Crowned (Stefan II Nemanjić)
rulers.title: Grand Prince; King from 1217
rulers.note: 'Returns to the throne in Ras in 1204'; 'Crowned King and Autocrat of all Serbian and coastal lands' in 1217; death 24 September 1228.

rulers.name: Stefan Radoslav
rulers.note: Start from the 1228 death of his father (S2). The Ivan Asen II page (opened for the Bulgarian dossier) has the Serbian nobles force him 'into exile in 1233'.

rulers.name: Stefan Vladislav I
rulers.note: Dates are the researcher's bridge: his start follows Radoslav's exile in 1233; the Uroš I page has 'from 1242 to spring 1243, a war for the throne' in which Uroš won the crown from Vladislav.

rulers.name: Stefan Uroš I
rulers.note: Coronation 1243 (infobox); 'Stefan Dragutin finally demanded the throne in 1276'.

rulers.name: Stefan Dragutin
rulers.note: Abdicated 'in favour of his younger brother Milutin, in 1282' (Serbian Kingdom page); then King of Srem (a separate state).

rulers.name: Stefan Uroš II Milutin
rulers.note: Accession 1282 (Serbian Kingdom page). End 1321 is implied by Dečanski's reign 1321-1331 on the same page; the Milutin page opened gives no death year.

rulers.name: Stefan Uroš III Dečanski
rulers.note: 'Dečanski's reign 1321-1331' (Serbian Kingdom page); on 21 August 1331 he surrendered to Dušan.

rulers.name: Stefan Dušan
rulers.title: King; Emperor from 16 April 1346
rulers.note: 'Crowned King of All Serbian and Maritime lands in the first week of September' 1331; the imperial reign belongs to serbian-empire.

wars.name: Nemanja's war with Byzantium and the Battle of the South Morava

zones.text: Niš and the South Morava valley, Byzantine Skopje

wars.outcome: Nemanja, allied with Béla III in 1183, attacked Byzantium, met Barbarossa at Niš in July 1189, took Skopje's direction in 1190 and was defeated by Isaac II on the South Morava (1191); the peace of 1193 had Stefan marry a Byzantine princess. The war began in 1183 under grand-principality-of-serbia (the page: Nemanja, allied with Béla III in 1183); it is dated here from 1188, the start of this state.
wars.note: The page dates the battle 1191 and Isaac's expedition 1190; it does not say which lands changed hands in 1193.

wars.name: Bulgarian invasion of Serbia and the brothers' war
wars.outcome: Vukan drove Stefan out in 1202 (to Kaloyan); Stefan returned in 1204 and the brothers' fighting stopped in 1205; Kaloyan took Niš in 1203.
wars.note: Niš from the Second Bulgarian Empire page, 1203.

wars.name: Serbo-Ragusan war (1252-1254)
wars.outcome: 'In 1252-1253, Uroš I was at war with the Republic of Ragusa' (allied with Bulgaria); 'Peace was ensured in a charter dated May 22, 1254.' No border moved.
wars.note: A second war in the later 1260s ended with the Ragusan tribute treaty of 1268.

wars.name: Serbian invasion of Mačva (1268)
wars.outcome: Uroš I invaded the Hungarian possessions in Mačva, was captured and paid for his release.

wars.name: Dragutin's revolt (1276)
wars.outcome: Dragutin demanded the throne in 1276 and, with Hungarian help, Uroš abdicated and retired to Hum; Dragutin abdicated for Milutin in 1282 and became King of Srem.
wars.note: The Hungarian help and the retirement to Hum are on the Uroš I page; Syrmia as a state dates from 1282-1284.

wars.name: Milutin's Macedonian war with Byzantium
wars.outcome: Milutin took northern Macedonia and Skopje in 1282, reached Kavala in 1283 and kept the conquests in the 1299 peace as the dowry of Simonis; Skopje became the capital.

wars.name: War between Dečanski and Vladislav II
wars.outcome: Rudnik was held by Dečanski's officials by the end of 1323; Vladislav was beaten in late 1324 and fled to Hungary.

wars.name: Bosnian conquest of Hum (1326)
wars.outcome: 'By the end of the same year, Serbia lost the region of Hum to Bosnia.'
wars.note: The Serbian Kingdom page says 'between 1322 and 1326'; the Bosnian dossier adds the 1329 fight at Priboj.

wars.name: Battle of Velbazhd (1330)
wars.outcome: Dečanski 'defeated and killed Michael Asen III in the Battle of Velbazhd (1330)'; Bulgaria lost no land (Velbazhd page, opened for the Bulgarian dossier) and Serbia advanced in Macedonia.

wars.name: Dušan's Macedonian war (1331-1334)
wars.outcome: Peace of 26 August 1334: the Byzantines recognised Serbian gains in Ohrid, Prilep, Strumitsa, Siderokastron, Chermen and Prosek.

wars.name: Dušan's offensive in the Byzantine civil war

zones.text: Macedonia as far as Kavala, without Thessaloniki

wars.outcome: Macedonia as far as Kavala without Thessaloniki; Serres on 25 September 1345; Dušan crowned Emperor at Skopje on 16 April 1346.

certainty.note: Medieval frontiers of the Nemanjić state are approximate throughout. The nearest to sharp are the lines named in treaties: the 1299 Byzantine peace (Milutin keeps his conquests) and the 26 August 1334 peace (Ohrid, Prilep, Strumitsa, Siderokastron, Chermen, Prosek), and the coastal sales to Ragusa (Ston, 1333).

notes:
Cliopatria row split. The row 'Kingdom of Serbia' (1188..1884, 19 shapes) is two states. Its first 18 shapes (1188-1351) are the medieval Nemanjic kingdom, written here under the bare slug kingdom-of-serbia, running 1188-1346 (a continuation of grand-principality-of-serbia, whose dossier ends 1187 and asks for a hand-over in 1188). The shape of 1880-1884 is the 1882-1918 kingdom; it is marked wrong here and belongs to the 'serbs' dossier (eu-18-f) with the 1885 outline. No new slug was needed: the modern state has its dossier. The wikipedia field of the Cliopatria row ('Kingdom of Serbia') and probably its Wikidata id Q241748 refer to the 1882-1918 article; this dossier points at 'Serbian Kingdom (medieval)', the article opened, and keeps Q241748 as Cliopatria gives it. The orchestrator may replace it.
The royal title: the kingdom starts in 1217 on the page; the dossier starts in 1188 with the 1217 rename, so that the colour is one from the grand principality to the empire (rule 2). The serbian-empire dossier starts in April 1346, so the two overlap only for 1346; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Serbia shape of 1333 (to 1351) is therefore kept for 1333 only and the empire carries 1346-1351.
Could not settle: (1) Hum: the Stefan page has Andrew of Hungary conquer 'Hum (Hercegovina) of grand zoupan Stefan' in 1198, yet Hum is Serbian again by 1326 and Cliopatria keeps it throughout; no opened page dates the return, so no 1198 event was entered (a gap-filler should open the Zahumlje page). (2) Niš: Serbian in July 1189 (Nemanja page) and 'the Serbs' were pushed out in 1203 (Second Bulgarian Empire page), while the Byzantine dossier says Bulgaria took Niš in 1191 and Cliopatria's Bulgarian shape includes it from 1192; the Niš union in the 1188 and 1192 keyframes follows the Serbian pages. (3) Growth in 1216 (Kosovo), 1220-1226 (the Skopje country) and 1250 (the Niš country): the pages are silent; entered at confidence 1 with Bulgaria as counterpart (the cells lie in Cliopatria's Bulgarian shapes, checked with the gazetteer). Cliopatria's Mačva and Belgrade cells for 1250-1284 contradict the pages (Hungarian possessions in 1268 and 1282) and are removed in the 1250 and 1272 verdicts. (4) Zeta 1204-1216 as a lighter tint is a reading. (5) The Milutin page has northern Albania and Durrës in 1284 and Durrës again in 1296; only 1296 is entered. (6) Braničevo: 1291 annexed by Dragutin (Milutin page), 'Milutin held control in Braničevo' in 1319; the Syrmia dossier cites 1292. (7) The Serbian Kingdom page is inconsistent about Dečanski (war of Macedonian conquest 'in 1331' but overthrown 21 August 1331). (8) 'Albania' under the 1343 title is undated on the Dušan page. (9) Reign dates of Radoslav and Vladislav I are bridges (see the ruler notes). (10) Ras's coordinates are the gazetteer's historic-site placeholder (20.6 E, 43.12 N).
Mirrors the other dossiers should carry: second-bulgarian-empire (gain of Niš 1203, loss of Kosovo 1216, the 1250 loss), byzantine-empire (loss of northern Macedonia in 1282, not 1285; the 1334 peace), kingdom-of-hungary (Mačva contest 1268, gain 1319, loss 1335), kingdom-of-syrmia (its 1324/1325 contest dates differ from the 1323/1324 here; the 1316 conquest), house-of-anjou-sicily (Durrës lost 1296, regained 1304), republic-of-ragusa (Ston and Pelješac 1333), banate-of-bosnia (Hum 1326, already there).
Pages that did not load: Stefan_Uroš_I_of_Serbia, Stefan_Uroš_II_Milutin, Stefan_Uroš_III_Dečanski (both with and without percent-encoding); the shorter titles used instead are in the sources.
Gazetteer names needed: Ston and Pelješac (a coordinate radius was used), Zeta (Podgorica radius used), Siderokastron/Sidirokastro, Chermen and Prosek (not drawn).
Budget: 9 pages opened (the Second Bulgarian Empire article counts as the ninth).

Fix pass 2026-11-01 (review eu-18-c). (1) Syrmia: option (a) taken: the 1316 conquest stands (Milutin page), a 1321 loss to kingdom-of-syrmia is added (Vladislav II freed at Milutin's death, 29 October 1321; Vladislav II and Dečanski pages), the 1324 gain stays; keyframes _1316, _1319, _1321 and _1324 draw it and _1314 is adjust for 1314-1315. kingdom-of-syrmia (its owner) still holds the land 1316-1325 without a loss: it needs a 1316 loss and a 1321 gain with counterpart kingdom-of-serbia. The Dečanski page names only Rudnik for the 1324 settlement ('By year's end, Rudnik was restored to Dečanski') and not Syrmia itself. (2) Skopje country: the Skopje page gives Skopje to Epirus 1214-1230, so Skopje itself is out of the 1220 gain, the 1227 loss and the _1220 shape; the strip north of it follows Cliopatria (Serbia 1220-1226, Bulgaria from 1227, confidence 1, now mirrored in second-bulgarian-empire). (3) Niš country 1250: mirrored in second-bulgarian-empire at confidence 1; no page dates it. (4) Bulgarian suzerainty over Serbia 1230-1241 mirrored here at confidence 1; the Vladislav page says no contemporary source has it, so it is a bridge. (5) Rudnik 1301 and 1312 mirrored from kingdom-of-syrmia. (6) 1329: the Dušan page has Serbia winning the battle of 1329 and the Ban taking over Nevesinje soon after (no year); the loss of Nevesinje and Zagorje is entered at 1329, confidence 2, and the 1326 Hum loss is narrowed by that circle; the Dečanski page has nothing on 1329. (7) Split of Syrmia dated 1284 to match the Syrmia dossier; the Dragutin page dates his separate kingdom from 1282 and his lands: northern Serbia with Rudnik, the Lim lands; the Hungarian grant of Mačva, Usora and Soli came in the second half of 1284. (8) Vukan Nemanjić added to the rulers 1202-1203; the first war starts in 1188 (it began in 1183). (9) Open for gap-fillers: Kosovo 1216, Zeta, the end of the 1268 contest, Durrës 1304 and the return of Hum before 1326 stay at confidence 1 or unentered. Also: banate-of-bosnia /ledger/6 (1324 gain of Usora and Soli from kingdom-of-serbia) has no Serbian side, because the Syrmia dossier gives Usora and Soli to Bosnia in 1325 and Cliopatria's Syrmia shape holds none of Tuzla.

Thin items re-read in the fix pass: Kosovo 1216 (Prizren page: Nemanjić control only 1219-20, confidence stays 1), Zeta 1204 (confidence 2 on the Vukan page; its end in 1216 is not on that page), the 1268 contest end (Uroš I page: a peace treaty, no year, confidence stays 1), Durrës (the Albania page has it Byzantine from 1288, so the 1296 counterpart is now byzantine-empire at confidence 2, and the 1304 expulsion is on the page, confidence 3). Hum: the Zachlumia page has Hungary conquering Hum in March 1198 (Andrew II), Radoslav of Zahumlje 'from 1254 a vassal of Hungary, but probably afterwards his land were absorbed into Serbia', and Milutin's war with Mladen Šubić ending with 'eastern Hum returned to him' ('After this agreement in 1313 the Neretva again became the border between eastern and western Hum'), then the Bosnian conquest 'in 1322-1326'; Cliopatria's Serbian shapes hold Hum throughout, so no event is entered and the return of eastern Hum (by 1313) stays a gap for a state dossier of Hum. Open: the 1282 split year (see above), the Syrmia owner's mirrors (1316 loss, 1321 gain), byzantine-empire's 1296 loss of Durrës.
